ai_summary: Aarti Industries reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA in Q2 FY27, driven by robust volume growth, resilient export demand, and strategic capacity expansions, including the commissioning of Zone IV and new long-term contracts. However, significant raw material cost inflation and geopolitical tensions led to soaring working capital and a net debt exceeding Rs. 4,650 crore, necessitating a Rs. 1,000 crore capital raise to deleverage the balance sheet. This material impact on financial health, alongside potential Q3 imported raw material supply chain gaps and delayed project stabilization, presents key challenges despite strong operational performance.
